text:
marta: Heads-up — product asked for a way to express 'SLO-driven routing' per customer tier + region with automatic fallback to cheaper model variants when latency SLOs break. Thinking about circuit-breaker thresholds in the router.
ken: +1 we need this for Dedicated customers hitting spikes. Are we thinking percentiles (p95) or tail-latency windows?
liam: p95 is common, but SLO windows + error budget consumption make more sense. e.g. if p95 > 400ms for 5m window, trigger fallback.
sabrina: UX question: do we expose raw thresholds in the Console or provide presets per tier (startup / standard / enterprise)? presets would reduce confusion. :thinking_face:
marta: presets + advanced override. Default tiers: dev, production, enterprise. Each preset maps to {latency_target_ms, availability_target_pct, cb_threshold_pct}.
ken: Also need region awareness — fallback in us-west shouldn't route to eu-central without opt-in. Policy should allow fallback within region then cross-region as last resort.
liam: Agree. Routing policy sketch (draft):
```
{
  "priority": ["tier", "region"],
  "slo": {"latency_ms": 300, "availability_pct": 99.9},
  "circuit_breaker": {"window_mins": 5, "p95_threshold_ms": 450, "open_if_pct_exceed": 0.2},
  "fallback_chain": ["quantized_variant", "smaller_model", "cross_region"],
  "fail_open": false
}
```
marta: Important: 'open_if_pct_exceed' is % of requests in window that exceed threshold?
liam: Yes — e.g., if >20% of requests in 5m have p95 > threshold, CB trips for that tier/region/model combo.
ken: Question: should circuit-breakers be per-route (API key / customer route) or global per-tier? per-route gives precision but many more metrics to track.
sabrina: From Console POV, per-customer (route) is what enterprise teams expect. We can coalesce thresholds to tier-level defaults and allow route-level overrides.
routing-bot: Metric alert created: routing.slo.p95_exceed for policy_id=draft-2026-03-18 (inc: #4321).
marta: Telemetry: we need token-level sampling so we can backfill when a CB trips to analyze error budget burn. Also add a small fingerprint (model_variant, quant, hw_type, region).
liam: + add a telemetry tag for 'fallback_reason' so logs show whether fallback was latency, availability, or capacity.
ken: API debate — do we model this as a distinct resource (RoutingPolicy) with its own CRUD endpoints, or as part of CustomerConfig?
sabrina: I vote RoutingPolicy resource. Benefits: versioning, rollouts (canary other policy), audit trail, and reuse across customers. Console can show a policy library.
marta: Rollouts: we should support canarying a new RoutingPolicy to X% of traffic and automatic rollback if CB opens. Also manual lock to prevent autopilot for enterprise customers.
liam: Implementation note: router must be able to evaluate policy with minimal added latency. Keep evaluation deterministic and O(1) per request (precompiled matchers + cached policy per token).
ken: Storage: policies in config store, policy versions in ddb + shadow copies in router local cache. When policy changes, publish a dirty key and let router refresh asynchronously with TTL.
sabrina: Console mock: show lane diagram — SLO bars, real-time p95, current CB state (closed/half-open/open) per region/tier. Allow 'open' to show last trigger events and sampled traces.
marta: We also need guardrails around fallback order: e.g. avoid repeated cross-region fallbacks when a region is unhealthy — prefer model downgrades first.
liam: For model variant fallback, include a quality score delta so product can display expected quality change. e.g. quantized_variant: -3 BLEU, smaller_model: -7 BLEU. (not exact metrics but relative).
ken: Cost implications: Enterprise might want to disable cost-based fallbacks. Add policy flag 'allow_cost_fallback': true/false.
sabrina: UX: add 'simulate' button in policy editor to run a synthetic spike and show hypothetical fallback sequence. This would help support explainability.
marta: Action items: (1) ken + liam to prototype routing-policy schema + router eval perf test by EOD Fri. (2) sabrina to sketch Console presets & mockups. (3) liam to add telemetry tags + routing-bot metric hooks.
ken: noted. I'll start with schema and a small loadtest.
liam: I'll add telemetry PR and a simple circuit-breaker lib we can embed in router.
sabrina: I'll drop mock screens in #design and link to this thread.
routing-bot: Reminder: please link design doc when ready — doc.create routing-policy-guardrails-draft (ID: rp-2026-03-18). :robot_face:
marta: Thanks all — let's sync tomorrow for 30m to review prototypes. :thumbsup:
